subject.title: Feature: Private Mode for demos and content creation

question: What exact no-read/no-write guarantee and activation scope should OpenClaw promise for private sessions?
rationale: Maintainers must choose allowed metadata, providers, tools, logs, workspace access, restart behavior, channel authorization, and toggle authority before implementation can safely encode the boundary.

options.title: Full ephemeral session
options.body: Guarantee no workspace or memory reads and no durable content writes across transcripts, plugins, tools, media, and UI history, accepting loss on restart.

options.title: Transcript-only privacy
options.body: Suppress transcript and memory persistence while allowing selected reads and operational metadata under a narrower documented promise.

options.title: Demo context mode
options.body: Only suppress persona and bootstrap context for screen-sharing without claiming durable privacy.

recommendation.title: Full ephemeral session
recommendation.body: Guarantee no workspace or memory reads and no durable content writes across transcripts, plugins, tools, media, and UI history, accepting loss on restart.

likelyOwner.reason: The current canonical session storage/UI boundary and prior cross-surface review are both tied to this owner.
